question: The average weight (in kg) of a family of five members whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 73 kg and 39 kg is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed average be 50 kg.

Deviations of each weight from 50 kg: −10, −1, +6, +23, −11

Net sum of deviations = (−10 − 1 + 6 + 23 − 11) = +7

Average deviation = +7 ÷ 5 = +1.4 kg

Actual average = Assumed average + Average deviation = 50 + 1.4 = 51.4 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 51.4 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weights of the 5 family members are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 73 kg, and 39 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 40
 
 
 
 49
 
 
 
 56
 
 
 
 73
 
 
 
 39
 
 
 
• 
 Average = 51.4
 
 
 Weights of 5 Family Members (kg)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of the family = 40 + 49 + 56 + 73 + 39

⇒ Total weight = 257 kg

⇒ Total number of members = 5

⇒ Average weight = 257 ÷ 5

⇒ Average weight = 51.4 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 51.4 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When different sets have different number of items, their combined average is calculated as: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Change in Average

If a constant 'k' is added, subtracted, multiplied or divided to each observation, the new average also undergoes the exact same operation by 'k'.

Finding an Included Item

Value of the newly added item = Old Average + (New Average − Old Average) × New Total Number of Items.
